chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah and Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said concerning a man who did not find water, and the salat (prayer) became due, so he performed tayammum and prayed two rakʿahs, then found water: does he invalidate the two rakʿahs, or cut them off and perform wudu (ablution) and then pray? He said: “No, rather he continues in his salat (prayer) and does not invalidate it, because he entered it while in a state of taharah (ritual purity) by tayammum.”

Zurārah said: So I said to him: He entered into it while in tayammum, then prayed one rakʿah and broke wudu, then found water. He said: “He goes out, performs wudu (ablution), and builds upon what has passed of his salat (prayer) which he prayed with tayammum.”

And the like of that is not binding in the case of one who has wudu (ablution), such that when he prays and then breaks wudu he may build upon what has passed of his salat (prayer), because the shariʿah has prevented that. That is because there is no disagreement among our companions that whoever breaks wudu during the salat (prayer) with that which cuts off his prayer, it is obligatory upon him to begin it anew; and this also indicates it.

key_terms.أَحْدَثَ: he entered a state of hadath that breaks ritual purity
key_terms.اسْتِئْنَافُهَا: restarting the prayer from the beginning
key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: dry ablution used in place of water-based purification
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water required for wudu when available
key_terms.يَبْنِي: he continues upon and completes what has already been performed

ai.seo_question: If someone starts salat with tayammum and then finds water, should he stop and perform wudu?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses rulings of tayammum during salat (prayer) when water becomes available. It states that one who began prayer in valid taharah (ritual purity) through tayammum continues the prayer, while a later discussion addresses the case of hadath during prayer and distinguishes it from the ruling of one who had entered with ordinary wudu (ablution).
